name: HGH Fragment 176-191
lead: HGH Fragment 176-191 (also written hGH frag 176-191 or "frag") is a synthetic peptide that corresponds to the final sixteen amino acids at the C-terminal end of the 191-residue human growth hormone molecule. It is sold online as a research chemical and is discussed in bodybuilding and fat-loss forums as a way to obtain growth hormone's fat-mobilising action without its growth-promoting effects.[1][2]

The idea behind the product comes largely from research on AOD9604, a modified version of the same segment that was tested in humans. Wikipedia notes that the unmodified fragment has been presented as lipolytic by extrapolation from AOD9604 data and that, unlike AOD9604, it has not itself been studied in humans.[1] Published work on the fragment is mostly laboratory and animal research, and it is not approved as a medicine.[1][2]
In community discussion it appears in bodybuilding contest-prep logs alongside other peptides, stimulants and thyroid hormone, usually as an add-on for cutting phases.[3][4][5]

paras: Human growth hormone (hGH) is a 191-amino-acid protein made by the anterior pituitary. Fragment 176-191 reproduces its terminal segment. Commercial versions are described as having an extra tyrosine at the N-terminus and a disulfide bridge between two cysteine residues that gives the peptide a cyclic shape.[2] This differs from AOD9604, which is the same region with a tyrosine added and is the version that entered clinical development.[1]

The peptide is made by solid-phase peptide synthesis and purified by chromatography, according to Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia whose content should be treated cautiously.[2] Suppliers are unregulated gray-market sources, and the purity and identity of vials have not been independently audited in the literature reviewed here.

The proposed rationale is that the C-terminal region of growth hormone carries the hormone's lipolytic (fat-breakdown) activity, so a fragment could stimulate fat metabolism without the receptor-mediated effects that raise IGF-1 and impair glucose handling.[2] Descriptions of this mechanism rest mainly on rodent work and on studies of AOD9604, and the receptor pathway has not been clearly defined.[2][6]

A 2001 paper titled as a comparison of the effects of hGH and its lipolytic fragment AOD9604 on lipid metabolism, and a 2000 paper on oral administration of a synthetic hGH fragment, are the kind of animal studies cited in support of the lipolytic idea.[6][7]
No studies found of HGH Fragment 176-191 itself in humans. Wikipedia states that, in contrast to AOD9604, the unmodified fragment has not been studied in humans.[1]

Related research: AOD9604, the modified analogue, has been tested in human trials, and Wikipedia describes the fat-loss claims for the unmodified fragment as extrapolated from that data.[1] A 2022 laboratory study used the fragment as a component of doxorubicin-loaded chitosan nanoparticles and reported increased toxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells in culture; this concerned drug delivery in cell culture and not fat loss.[8] No registered clinical trial of the exact peptide was found.

Because the exact peptide has not been studied in people, no human safety profile has been published. It is not approved by regulators for any medical use and is distributed as a research chemical.[1][2] Grokipedia states that studies of AOD9604 reported no effect on IGF-1 or glucose tolerance, but this concerns the modified analogue rather than the fragment sold online.[2]

Growth hormone fragments are listed among the substances prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency, according to a first-pass summary of the topic; competitors in tested sports are therefore subject to anti-doping rules.

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities
paras: On T Nation, discussions from 2008 onward mention the fragment as an adjunct for fat loss during contest preparation, often together with GH secretagogues such as GHRP-6, CJC-1295 or sermorelin, and with clenbuterol, ECA stacks or T3.[3][4][5][9][10] Users share anecdotal logs, and some posts ask for advice on how to use it, which this article does not reproduce. Posters also note uncertainty about whether physicians would prescribe it.[4]
Reports in these threads are self-reported and uncontrolled, and combine the fragment with other agents, so they do not isolate its effect.

lore.intro: Bodybuilding forums such as T Nation present the fragment as a fat-loss peptide used in cutting phases, usually alongside other agents.[3][5]

claims.claim: Frag 176-191 is the part of growth hormone that burns fat, without the other GH effects
claims.believers: Forum posters describe the fragment as the chain of growth hormone responsible for fat loss and use it in results logs and contest preparation.[3][9]
claims.experts: Wikipedia says the lipolytic reputation was extrapolated from data on AOD9604 and that the unmodified fragment has not been studied in humans.[1]

claims.claim: Stacking it with GH secretagogues, clenbuterol or T3 improves fat loss
claims.believers: Contest-prep posters report combining the fragment with GHRP-6, CJC-1295, clenbuterol or T3 in the final weeks before a show.[4][5][10]
claims.experts: No published study has tested such combinations; reports are anecdotal and confounded by simultaneous agents.

claims.claim: It is safe because it does not raise IGF-1 or blood sugar
claims.believers: Proponents argue the fragment lacks the growth-promoting actions of full-length hGH.[2]
claims.experts: Data on lack of IGF-1 effect come from studies of the modified analogue AOD9604, and no human safety data exist for the unmodified peptide sold online.[1][2]
